processing: The details of its making are little documented. As with other regional Guizhou greens, expect fresh leaf to be heat-fixed, shaped and dried without oxidation.
harvest_season: Around Qingming in early April, from overwintered buds that formed the previous autumn and fill out in spring.
appearance_dry: Little is recorded about the dry leaf; the leaf is described as plump and soft, so expect a fuller, greener leaf than a fine bud tea.
appearance_liquor: Not specifically described; a clear yellow-green is typical of Guizhou spring greens.
taste_profile: Rich and mellow in aroma and flavour, clean in the mouth, with a sweet return and good staying power over repeat steeps.

brewing.notes: General guidance for a spring green rather than a recorded local method. The thicker leaf takes repeat steeps well; lower the temperature if the cup turns sharp.

vintage_note: The name itself points to the season: this is a Qingming-time picking. As with other Chinese greens it is usual to buy the current spring harvest and drink it within the year; it is not a tea for ageing.
description:
Leishan Qingming Tea is a green tea from Leishan county in southeast Guizhou, grown in the Leigongshan nature reserve at about 1300 to 1400 metres. It is listed among Guizhou's regional public brands, and its fuller local name advertises selenium.

The idea behind it is seasonal. Buds that formed the autumn before sit through the winter and develop around Qingming, and that slow build-up is credited with the thick, soft leaf this tea is known for. Its making is little documented, so treat it as a regional green in the broad sense.

Expect a rich, mellow cup with a clean finish and a sweet return, and more staying power than delicate bud teas usually have. Start at around 85°C with moderate steeps and adjust from there.

The selenium is the selling point: local descriptions give 2.00 to 2.02 micrograms per gram and call that 15 times the ordinary tea average. Treat that as a producer-side figure rather than a reason to buy. When buying, ask for the harvest date, because freshness will matter more to the cup.
history: Little is documented about when this tea took its present form. What is recorded is its place in Guizhou's list of regional brands, alongside Leishan Yinqiu from the same county.
